clue.text: Tradition about it? Don't ask a lady this

indicators.note: about means going round, so the lady's unaskable question wraps the little word it

parts.note: etiquette says you never ask a woman how old she is, so this is her age
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gallant question about an old custom, followed by a reminder of the one thing a gentleman never asks a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'Don't ask a lady this' look like a separate remark, but it is a phrase standing for HER AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A heritage is what is handed down from earlier generations, which is what a tradition is.

clue.text: He gets much bigger party decorations

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
to balloon is to swell up greatly

explanation.surface: A man who puts on a lot of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a person, but it is the chemical symbol, spelled out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas-filled floating balloons are a classic decoration at children's parties.

clue.text: Flick switch, one in show

indicators.note: in places one inside the turned switch
to flick something over is to turn it, so the switch word is read backwards

parts.note: a lever is a switch
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Instructions for turning on a light at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show it, uncovering it to view.

clue.text: Travel over hot rocks to get this signature

indicators.note: over means the travel word spreads over and encloses the other pieces

parts.note: to travel round is to tour
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a reef is a ridge of rocks in the sea

explanation.surface: A firewalker's feat, crossing hot stones for a signature trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The signature is a time signature in music, three beats of crotchets to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-four is the musical time signature with three crotchet beats per bar, as in a waltz.

clue.text: Forward information about pitch of instrument

indicators.note: about means the information wraps round the forward

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a lock is a forward in rugby union
a sales pitch is a spiel

explanation.surface: A forward player passing on news about the state of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' and 'pitch' suggest sport; LOCK is a rugby forward position and the pitch is a sales spiel.
explanation.definitionFit: The glockenspiel is a percussion instrument of tuned metal bars struck with hammers.

clue.text: Light meat packed with energy

indicators.note: packed with means the meat has something stuffed inside it

parts.note: bacon is a cured meat
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A healthy-eating note that a certain meat is full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire or lamp, a kind of light used to warn or guide.

clue.text: He painted birds head to toe

indicators.note: head to toe means the first letter is moved down to the end

parts.note: terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: An artist who painted birds from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter, so he is a man who painted.

clue.text: Provide entertainment outside the tube

indicators.note: outside means the entertainment word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to cater is to provide food and entertainment for guests
taken as written

explanation.surface: A host laying on entertainment outside the Underground station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tube' suggests the London Underground, but the tube is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a thin flexible medical tube inserted into the body.

clue.text: Switch current after number 12

indicators.note: after puts the switch and current pieces behind the number

parts.note: on is a position of a switch
a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: An electrical instruction to change the current after a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is an old word for midday, when the clock shows twelve.

clue.text: Livestock disease potentially shocking — man of God to return

parts.note: a live wire can give you an electric shock
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

indicators.note: return means the little word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: An alarming farm disease, and a clergyman summoned back to deal with it.
explanation.walkthrough: RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver rot is a fluke infestation of sheep and cattle, so a disease of farm animals.

clue.text: Slick passing move's testing Mike

definitions.meaning: in football, a quick give-and-go between two players
what a sound engineer says into a microphone (a mike) to check it works

explanation.walkthrough: Mike is a short form of microphone, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a quick football pass-and-return and the count spoken when checking a microphone.

clue.text: Wordsmith thus honoured with epaulette or a buckle?

indicators.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer receiving an honour wonders whether it comes with an epaulette or a buckle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poet Laureate is a poet officially honoured by appointment to the royal household.

clue.text: Custom banger lacks it up front

indicators.note: lacks says something is missing from the banger
up front places the missing letters at the start of the word

parts.note: banger is British slang for a sausage
it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain sausage is missing something at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention; banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established practice or habit, the same as custom.

clue.text: Most difficult bird to draw on street

parts.note: the knot is a wading bird
in sport, to draw is to tie

explanation.surface: Instructions to sketch a bird on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching; here it means finishing level, to tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a hard one, so knottiest is the hardest of all.

clue.text: Death claims bishop after drinks and crackers

indicators.note: after puts the death-and-bishop part behind the drinks

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

indicators.note: claims means taking hold of, so death encloses the bishop

parts.note: death is the end
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A grim tale of a bishop dying after a session of drinks and crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: Round the bend is British slang for mad, the same idiom as crackers.

clue.text: Always outside, stealing a kiss

indicators.note: stealing means the kiss is taken away from the outside word

parts.note: externally means on the outside
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A romantic always out of doors, snatching a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever, without end, the same as always.

clue.text: Target of peculiar rubbing

indicators.note: peculiar means strange, so the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: Someone singled out for a strange rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Frottage is an art technique of taking a rubbing from a textured surface, pioneered by Max Ernst.

clue.text: It determines the value of amended dictates

indicators.note: amended means changed, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A test that weighs the worth of revised commands.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test, originally assaying gold with nitric acid, is a decisive test of worth.

clue.text: Spinner of 78's first prize held by most productive hen

indicators.note: held by means the prize letter sits inside the hen phrase

parts.note: a hen that lays more eggs than any other is a record layer

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word prize

explanation.surface: A champion egg-laying hen wins first prize.
explanation.walkthrough: '78's first' looks like a phrase, but the definition ends at 78's; 'first prize' is the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A 78 is an old shellac disc, and the machine that spins it is a gramophone.

clue.text: Bad tempered animal bites master's foot

indicators.note: bites means the animal holds the other letter in its jaws

parts.note: a moose is a large deer

indicators.note: foot picks the bottom letter, the last one, of master

explanation.surface: A grumpy creature that nips its owner's foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, so ill-humoured.

clue.text: Plant on base of hatstand

indicators.note: base of picks the bottom letter, the last one, of hat

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A pot plant put on the bottom of a hatstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hatstand' must be split: the base of 'hat' gives T, and 'stand' gives EASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasel is a prickly plant whose dried heads were once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Time to remake bed — ready to give him a cuddle?

indicators.note: remake means the letters are made up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Bedtime routine: tidy the bed, then hug the toy waiting there.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'him', given meaning by the whole clue: the one you are ready to cuddle once the bed is made.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with the rest of the clue, him is the cuddly toy bear that sits on a child's bed.

clue.text: It floats upriver, carrying children

indicators.note: carrying means the turned river holds the children
up in a down entry means the river name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A boat drifting upstream with children aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' must be split: 'up' turns the River Tay, Scotland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or pleasure boat, something that floats.

clue.text: Return shortly with ultimate picture hanger

indicators.note: Return means the word for shortly is read backwards

parts.note: shortly means soon

indicators.note: ultimate picks the final letter of the word picture

explanation.surface: A request to come back soon with the last item, a hook to hang a picture on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture hanger' looks like the definition, but 'picture' gives only its last letter; the hanger is a hangman's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is the rope loop used in hanging someone, so it is grimly a hanger.

clue.text: Insight gleaned from newspaper cutting

indicators.note: gleaned from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clever observation picked up from a clipping out of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a quick illuminating remark or glimpse, a flash of understanding.

clue.text: See 1 down
What's left of houses and car?

definitions.meaning: the property a person leaves behind at death
a British car with a long body and rear door, like a station wagon

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition. An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a dead person's assets, a development of homes, and a long-backed car.

clue.text: Fine light which signals spring

parts.note: a Very light is a flare fired from a Very pistol as a signal
a spring is a source of water, as is a well

explanation.surface: A bright signal flare that announces the arrival of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Very lights are signal flares named after their inventor Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: Very well is an expression of agreement meaning all right, so fine.
